I fixed both bugs and pushed the branch `fix/35-max-tokens-continuation` in four commits, but I couldn't open the PR. GitHub refused with "GitHub Actions is not permitted to create or approve pull requests". You can open it here: https://github.com/cv/pi-action/compare/main...fix/35-max-tokens-continuation. Neither open question blocked the work; my choices are below. `npm run check` (typecheck, lint, coverage, knip/jscpd) and the pre-push coverage hook pass.

**What changed**
- **`length` stops** (`src/conversation.ts`): the code now checks the stop reason of the last response, not just whether its text is empty. When a response is cut off at the token limit without a tool call, pi sends the continuation prompt from the issue, with tools still available.
- **Retry limit:** after 4 cut-offs in a row (the first plus 3 continuations), pi stops. If a continuation runs tools before being cut off again, the count resets. pi then posts an error comment that says the responses kept hitting the limit, suggests raising `model_max_tokens`, and includes the last partial text. It also logs a warning naming the input.
- **Partial text:** if a cut-off response has text, it's posted with a note that it was cut off and pi is continuing.
- **Timeout:** no continuation is sent once the run's `timeout` is reached.
- **Re-runs:** continuations have stable keys (`<key>-continue-<n>`), so a re-run gets the existing ones back instead of sending them again, and partial text isn't posted twice.
- **`SUMMARY_PROMPT`** now neutrally asks what was done, which files changed, what's left and any errors. It no longer says "you completed your work".
- **Tools in the summary prompt are now allowed.** An empty stop doesn't mean the work is done, and the old "do NOT call tools" pushed the model to give up. The model can now finish first but must still end with a text reply; if that's empty too, the existing "failed after two attempts" error is reported. The old ban was only a request in the prompt anyway.
- **README:** the `model_max_tokens` row now explains what happens when a response hits the limit.

**Tests:** I added 9 tests to `src/run.test.ts` (faux model), covering every case in the acceptance criteria. Extra ones cover the count reset after tool use, partial text in the give-up comment, and a later run not repeating continuations. There's no separate `src/conversation.test.ts`; all the new tests are in `run.test.ts`.

**Open questions**
- **Retry limit:** 3 continuations in a row, also bounded by the remaining `timeout`.
- **Default `model_max_tokens`:** left at 16384 and documented instead. Each provider caps it per model, so a higher default could break models with smaller limits.

`npm ci` reinstalled the git hooks and left `.legacy` copies that broke `prepare-commit-msg`. I deleted them on the runner only; nothing in the repo changed.

The PR description I wrote, to paste when you open it:

> Fixes #35.
>
> Looks at the stop reason of the last response after a prompt settles. A `length` stop with no tool call gets a continuation with tools allowed: up to 3 cut-offs in a row, and the count resets when a continuation uses tools. Continuations stop at the `timeout`. Past the limit, pi posts an error with the partial text and suggests raising `model_max_tokens`. Partial text from a cut-off response is posted, marked as cut off. Continuation keys are stable, so re-runs don't send them again.
>
> `SUMMARY_PROMPT` is now neutral (done / left / errors) and allows tools, because an empty stop doesn't mean the work is finished; the model must still end with a text reply.
>
> Decisions on the open questions: retry limit is 3 in a row, also bounded by `timeout`; the default stays 16384 and the README documents what happens at the limit.
>
> Tests are in `src/run.test.ts` and cover every acceptance case, plus the count reset, partial text in the give-up comment, and dedup on a later run. `npm run check` passes.
